thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p95 latency SLO breached on /v1/generate (us-east-1) — sustained >3m. auto-reroute: redwood-v3-full -> redwood-v2-quant. Pager: @irene oncall
irene: ack — paging in. jumping into dashboard now. who's on-call for routing policy?
sam: i'm here. seeing reroutes roughly every 18–22s, looks like the routing controller keeps flipping the route back and forth.
maria: also seeing spike in 502/timeout on the fallback (redwood-v2-quant). error rate on that variant goes up after the switch.
incident-bot: routing events (last 2m):
```
2025-07-21T01:02:18Z route /v1/generate us-east-1 from redwood-v3-full -> redwood-v2-quant (p95 breach)
2025-07-21T01:02:36Z route /v1/generate us-east-1 from redwood-v2-quant -> redwood-v3-full (p95 recovered)
2025-07-21T01:02:54Z route /v1/generate us-east-1 from redwood-v3-full -> redwood-v2-quant (p95 breach)
... repeated
```
sam: that pattern screams zero cooldown / too-tight hysteresis. controller flips as soon as p95 dips below threshold then back up.
irene: confirm current routing policy? post config snippet pls.
maria: here's the policy (from config service):
```
{"policy":"latency_slo","cooldown_seconds":0,"p95_threshold_ms":240,"max_failover_retries":3}
```
sam: cooldown_seconds=0 — that's the problem. should be 60–120s to avoid oscillation.
irene: immediate mitigation: 1) disable automated fallback 2) pin traffic to redwood-v3-full in us-east-1 3) scale up redwood-v3-full by +2 replicas — will do in that order. ping when done.
tim: manual pinning API call executed: `POST /internal/routing/pin` payload `{"route":"/v1/generate","region":"us-east-1","variant":"redwood-v3-full","duration_s":"900"}` — confirmed via audit logs.
lisa: scaling redwood-v3-full now: `kubectl scale deploy/redwood-v3-full --replicas=6 -n inference-us-east1` — replicas increased, pods warming.
maria: root cause addendum: redwood-v2-quant lacks optimized KV-cache for long-context ops; when it received a sudden rate of long-context traffic it started tail-latency spirals -> fallback amplified load back to primary -> flip.
incident-bot: Customer-impact update: 3 enterprise customers reported 30–45s tail latencies and a few 504s. CS notified those accounts at 01:10 UTC. No data exfiltration. Severity: P1.
cs-rep: pinged top accounts, providing workaround (set timeout=30s client-side) and ETA for stabilization.
pagerduty-bot: Escalation: SREs paged to conference bridge; @sam @maria @irene are on the call.
irene: ruling: keep routing automation disabled for us-east-1 while we validate variant health and update policy cooldown. sam, can you push a safe default?
sam: pushing change to config service: `cooldown_seconds=90`. Deploying now.
incident-bot: config patch applied and rolled to controllers. New policy snapshot:
```
{"policy":"latency_slo","cooldown_seconds":90,"p95_threshold_ms":240,"max_failover_retries":2}
```
maria: after pin + scale + cooldown change, p95 is trending back to normal. no additional flips in the last 4 minutes.
irene: good. next steps: 1) rollback redwood-v2-quant from production or tag it with 'no-fallback' until kv-cache fix 2) postmortem owner: sam 3) notify product + customers 4) schedule policy QA to prevent zero-cooldown pushes.
tim: created INC-2025-432 in tracker, severity P1, linked logs and config diffs.
lisa: taking on overnight monitoring for 3 hours and will update incident channel at +1h and +3h. handing off to @lisa for watch.
irene: handing off — @lisa you have the incident. I'll be reachable but stepping off. IR handoff notes: pinned, automation disabled, cooldown=90s, scale=+2, rollback plan ready.
lisa: ack — monitoring. will escalate if p95 goes above 280ms for >5m.
maria: quick log snippet showing the kv-cache misses during spike:
```
[2025-07-21T01:03:12Z] variant=redwood-v2-quant kv_cache_miss_rate=0.87 tail_latency_p95=620ms
[2025-07-21T01:03:30Z] variant=redwood-v2-quant error_502_rate=0.12
```
sam: follow-ups: create a policy guardrail in config service to reject cooldown_seconds < 30s for latency_slo policy, and add a canary test that exercises fallback variant under long-context load.
irene: agreed. postmortem due EOD tomorrow. Thanks team — big help getting this stabilized. :thumbsup:
